hero.tagline: Stand Down if you sedated Williams in Episode 5. Shoot if you skipped it — and accept a locked trophy.
hero.intro: The Point Blank standoff in Episode 6: what each option does, which trophy it unlocks or locks, and why the Episode 5 sedative decides the outcome.

options.heading: The Two Options at Point Blank

cards.title: Stand Down — hold fire
cards.body: Let the scan finish. If you sedated Williams in Episode 5, it identifies him as human and the standoff ends without a death.
cards.chain: ⟳ Unlocks **Suspect Acquitted**. Keeps the everyone-survives route alive.

cards.title: Shoot immediately
cards.body: Williams is shot at point-blank range. No guide surveyed for this page documents him surviving it.
cards.chain: ⟳ **Suspect Acquitted** is no longer available, and the everyone-survives route fails.

sceneContext.heading: What Leads Up to Point Blank?
sceneContext.summary: ⚠ Spoilers — click to expand the Episode 5 setup
paragraphs: Point Blank is the Williams standoff in **Episode 6**, not Episode 5. Stafford has Williams at gunpoint while the ship's scanner runs; the result decides whether the crew is facing the real Williams.

The outcome is set one episode earlier. In **Episode 5**, during the “Suspicions” section, Anders proposes sedating Williams so she can get into his computer. Agree to the plan and prepare the sedative — the diazepam synthesis uses code **168** — and Anders administers it in a coffee. That unlocks **Is This Decaf?** (“Sedated Williams”).
If Williams was not sedated, he is replaced by a **duplicate**. The scan cannot identify a duplicate as human, so **Suspect Acquitted** is out of reach for that playthrough.

outcomes.heading: What Happens If You Pick Each Option

columns.heading: Stand Down →
items: The scan identifies Williams as human — **if** you sedated him in Episode 5
Unlocks **Suspect Acquitted** (“Williams was identified as human”)
Without the Episode 5 sedative, the scan cannot confirm him

columns.heading: Shoot →
items: Williams is shot at point-blank range; no guide surveyed shows him surviving
**Suspect Acquitted** is no longer available in that playthrough
The everyone-survives route needs him alive in Episode 8, so it fails
No trophy or story benefit is documented for shooting

outcomes.outro: If you completed the Episode 5 sedation, Stand Down is the correct call: Williams is confirmed human and the trophy unlocks. If you skipped it, shooting ends the scene quickly — but Suspect Acquitted was already out of reach, and the shot removes Williams from the surviving crew.

faqs.q: Should you shoot Williams or stand down in Directive 8020?
faqs.a: Stand Down — if you sedated Williams in Episode 5. The scan then identifies him as human and unlocks Suspect Acquitted. Shooting forfeits the trophy for that playthrough.

faqs.q: What happens if you shoot Williams?
faqs.a: Williams is shot at point-blank range. Suspect Acquitted is no longer available in that playthrough, and the everyone-survives route fails because it needs him alive in Episode 8.

faqs.q: Which episode is the Williams standoff?
faqs.a: Episode 6. “Point Blank” is the standoff scene; the sedative setup happens one episode earlier, in Episode 5's “Suspicions” section.

faqs.q: How do you save Williams in Directive 8020?
faqs.a: Agree to Anders' sedation plan in Episode 5 and prepare the sedative (diazepam synthesis, code 168), then choose Stand Down at Point Blank in Episode 6. That unlocks Is This Decaf? and Suspect Acquitted.

faqs.q: Does standing down work without the sedative?
faqs.a: No. If Williams was not sedated in Episode 5, he is replaced by a duplicate and the scan cannot identify him as human, so Suspect Acquitted cannot unlock.
